name: Data Table
tagline: A sortable, filterable table over any Dataverse view, with inline editing, pinned columns and a New button.

limitations: Paging works against the fixture. The demo keeps the page between renders and takes a page size on the next fetch, as a form does, and the pager counts what the view holds. The fixture has 24 rows, so the Filtering and export preset asks for 10 a page to give the pager three pages; the other presets ask for 25, which is one. What it cannot show is a view too large to count: a real one can report totalResultCount as -1, and the pager then names the page rather than printing “of -1”.

Sorting reorders the rows. The control writes into dataset.sorting and calls refresh(), and the demo sorts the whole fixture on that fetch, the way a real view sorts on the server across every page rather than reordering the rows on screen. Multi-column sort is off by default; turned on, a second column joins dataset.sorting behind the first, and the demo applies every entry in order.

Clicking a row calls dataset.openDatasetItem(). There is no form behind this origin to open, so the event log under the demo names the record that would have opened instead. The openedRecordId output still updates, so the value a form would react to is visible.

Ticked rows survive a re-render: the demo keeps dataset.setSelectedRecordIds() as a form does, and the selectedRecordIds output follows it. On a model-driven form that same call is what tells the command bar which records the ribbon acts on; there is no command bar here to tell.

Filtering narrows the rows. The control calls dataset.filtering.setFilter() and then refresh(), and the demo applies the expression to the whole fixture on that fetch, as the server does across every page: text, numbers with comparisons such as >1000, dates On, From or Until a whole day, and Category from a select of its choices. The count under the table follows the filtered set. The filter row also shows which column types get a box and which deliberately do not.

Export CSV is on in the Filtering and export preset and builds a real file from the rows on the page — ten of them, since that preset pages by ten. The control hands it to navigation.openFile, as it does on a form; the demo cannot save a file from inside its sandbox, so the event log under the demo offers it as a Download. Set Export scope to the whole view and the control walks the pages instead and reassembles all 24 rows, as it would up to ten thousand on a real view, a page at a time. Afterwards it puts you back on the page you started from.

Inline editing works here, and the write is real — against the demo's stand-in Dataverse. The harness carries the write half of a dataset record (setValue, save, isEditable), so an edit commits, survives the next render and the table shows it, but nothing leaves the browser: Reset or a reload puts the fixture back as authored. Account number is marked read-only in the fixture on purpose, so you can see the half that matters — the control asks the platform whether each cell is writable, per column and per record, and renders a refused one as plain text rather than offering an editor it would then have to take back.

A refused write rolls back here, as on a form. The demo’s stand-in Dataverse refuses one change, the way a plugin would on a real environment: making an account a Preferred Customer. In the Inline editing preset, set a Standard account’s Category to Preferred Customer. The save is rejected, the cell returns to Standard, and the reason is named underneath it — the path this control exists to catch. Every other edit saves, including a Preferred Customer set to Standard, which then cannot be set back until Reset. The sentence is the fixture’s own; a write refused for a missing privilege carries the platform’s sentence instead and takes the same path.

Choice cells edit here, and choice columns filter. Category holds the account’s category as the integer Dataverse keeps, and the demo’s stand-in Dataverse describes its options, which the control reads through utils.getEntityMetadata as on a form: a Category cell opens a select of Preferred Customer and Standard, the choice is written like any other edit, and the filter row gives Category a select. The fixture shows Category rather than Status because a state or status column stays read-only on a form — the platform reports it so, and the control keeps it that way. The New button is drawn in the Inline editing preset, where Allow adding rows is on: it asks navigation.openForm for the table’s quick create form, and with no form behind the demo the event log names the form that would have opened and no row is added.

Pinned columns are layout, so they need no server and no dataset call, and what the Pinned columns preset shows is exactly what a form shows. A pinned column is only visible once there is something to scroll, so the fixture carries eight columns: pinned, the table asks for 940px, which is wider than this page gives it at any size. Switch to the Pinned columns preset and drag the scrollbar under the rows — Account name stays at the left edge, Modified on at the right, and everything between them passes behind. The one thing to try deliberately is the phone preview: below about 440px the pinned pair would leave nothing to scroll between them, so the control unpins itself rather than trap you, and that clamp is real behaviour rather than a demo shortcut.

Grouping runs here and its numbers are right, but by the browser route — the one a canvas app gets. The demo’s stand-in Dataverse does not answer FetchXML, so the server aggregate over the whole view is refused and the control groups the rows it has loaded instead. The caption under the table says which route answered. Here that costs nothing: the 24 rows fit on one page, so “the records loaded so far” is every record there is, and the counts and summed revenue are the numbers a server would return. On a view of four thousand rows that caption is the whole difference between a total and a page total. Opening a group works: it is a filter plus refresh(), which the demo applies, so the rows beneath it are that owner’s and the pager is scoped to them. While one is open the other groups leave the list, because the browser route can only group the rows the filter loaded; closing it brings them back. Group by Owner, City or Category. Category groups on its integer, as a real view groups a Choice, and each group takes its label from the options.

Primary contact is a lookup to contact, and editing it works against the demo's stand-in Dataverse by the same route as on a form. In the Inline editing preset, click a contact: Choose… opens a lookup dialog over the demo's contacts (utils.lookupObjects), the navigation property is read from the relationship metadata, and the write is a webAPI.updateRecord with @odata.bind followed by a refresh. Clear empties the cell the same way. The dialog is the demo's own searchable list rather than the platform's, with its views; media/screenshot-lookup.png is the real one, captured from the dev rig in this repository.

presets.name: Default
presets.description: An eight-column, 24-row view with sortable columns, a per-column filter row and multi-row selection.

presets.name: Grouped with totals
presets.description: Five owners, largest first, each with its record count and the revenue summed beneath it. Collapsed, the group list is the whole table — no member rows until you open one. Open one and its records load beneath it.

presets.name: Pinned columns
presets.description: Account name held at the start and Modified on at the end while the six between them scroll behind. Drag the scrollbar under the rows, then try the phone preview: the control unpins itself when the pair would leave nothing to scroll.

presets.name: Inline editing
presets.description: Click any cell to edit it — Primary contact opens a lookup. Account number is read-only in the fixture, so it stays plain text. Making an account a Preferred Customer is refused: the cell rolls back and says why. New opens a quick create.

presets.name: Filtering and export
presets.description: The filter row, CSV export and a rows-per-page picker at ten a page, showing which column types get a box — text, number, and since 0.4.0 a date picker with an On / From / Until chip — and which do not. The CSV file is offered in the event log.
